items.stem: Which of the following best describes "labour turnover"?
options: The way an organization is arranged in terms of roles, responsibilities, lines of authority and communication
An organizational structure with few levels of hierarchy and wide spans of control
A labour market in which workers are engaged for short-term tasks or "gigs", often through digital platforms, rather than permanent jobs
The percentage of employees who leave an organization during a period, usually a year
items.answer: The percentage of employees who leave an organization during a period, usually a year
items.markingKey: D. "labour turnover" is the percentage of employees who leave an organization during a period, usually a year.

items.stem: A hotel chain plans to open five new hotels next year, each needing 60 staff. It currently has 900 staff and expects labour turnover of 15%. Calculate the number of staff it must recruit next year and suggest one recruitment method.
items.answer: Replacements: 15% × 900 = 135; new staff: 5 × 60 = 300; total = 435. Method: online job platforms/careers website for large-volume recruitment, or internal promotion for supervisors.
items.markingKey: Replacements: 15% × 900 = 135; new staff: 5 × 60 = 300; total = 435. Method: online job platforms/careers website for large-volume recruitment, or internal promotion for supervisors.

items.stem: Tasman Surf Co. employed an average of 400 staff last year, and 90 employees left during the year. Each employee was expected to work 240 days, and 2,020 working days were lost through absence. Calculate the labour turnover rate and the absenteeism rate, and explain one cost to Tasman Surf Co. of high labour turnover.
items.answer: Labour turnover = 22.5%; absenteeism = 2,020/(400 × 240) × 100 = 2.10%. Cost: recruitment, induction and training of replacements, and lost productivity while new staff learn the job.
items.markingKey: LT = 90/400 × 100 = 22.5%; absenteeism = days lost / total possible days × 100 = 2.10%. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both rates. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [R1] relevant cost explained.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "delegation"?
options: The management of an organization's workforce, including workforce planning, recruitment, training, appraisal, motivation, dismissal and redundancy
Passing authority to a subordinate to carry out a task, while the manager retains overall responsibility
Working arrangements that vary hours or location, such as flexitime, part-time work, remote or hybrid working and compressed hours
The delegation of decision-making authority to lower levels or to regional or local managers
items.answer: Passing authority to a subordinate to carry out a task, while the manager retains overall responsibility
items.markingKey: B. "delegation" is passing authority to a subordinate to carry out a task, while the manager retains overall responsibility.

items.stem: Delta Drones has 5 levels of hierarchy, with each manager supervising 4 subordinates. The company plans to delayer by doubling the span of control to 8. Calculate the current number of employees, and the number of levels needed to employ at least the same number of people after delayering. Explain one benefit and one risk of delayering.
items.answer: Current employees = 341; with span 8, levels needed = 4. Benefit: faster communication and lower management costs; risk: managers overloaded, less supervision and fewer promotion opportunities.
items.markingKey: Total = Σ 4^k = 341; with span 8: cumulative 1, 1+8, ... ≥ 341 at 4 levels. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for 341 and 4 levels. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [R1] benefit; [R1] risk.

items.stem: Café Andino employed an average of 80 staff last year, and 6 employees left during the year. Each employee was expected to work 240 days, and 170 working days were lost through absence. Calculate the labour turnover rate and the absenteeism rate, and explain one cost to Café Andino of high labour turnover.
items.answer: Labour turnover = 7.5%; absenteeism = 170/(80 × 240) × 100 = 0.89%. Cost: recruitment, induction and training of replacements, and lost productivity while new staff learn the job.
items.markingKey: LT = 6/80 × 100 = 7.5%; absenteeism = days lost / total possible days × 100 = 0.89%. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both rates. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [R1] relevant cost explained.
